title: The Ten-Minute Meeting That Ran Three Hours and Became Genentech
conflicts: Kleiner Perkins calls Swanson 'a young partner' at the firm; Wikipedia says his job there ended by late 1975; story says he 'had worked at' the firm. MIT News says he founded Genentech at 29; he was born in 1947 (October), so 28 for most of 1976; story gives no age. Meeting place: Boyer's lab (Wikipedia) versus a beer (Kleiner Perkins, PBS); story uses both, attributing the beer to Kleiner Perkins, and does not name the bar. The $100,000 seed figure (Wikipedia only) and the $38.5 million IPO figure (PBS only) are left out.
notes: Sourcing is thinner than ideal: the shared web-search budget ran out mid-task, and the Bancroft oral histories (Calisphere renders by script), NYT and Guardian obituaries could not be read, so the story attributes no thoughts or feelings to either founder and sticks to documented facts from Genentech, Kleiner Perkins, PBS, the Science History Institute, MIT News and one Wikipedia page (supplementary). An editor may wish to enrich it from Sally Smith Hughes's oral histories. Quote stance: affirms.
